posts.title: Trapnest House: Spatial Mechanics
posts.description: A quiet digital sanctuary, built from camera kinematics, tactile objects, and the feeling of walking through a room.
posts.lead: What if a website were an actual room?
body: A room you can move through

Trapnest House turns the idea of a website into a navigable sanctuary. Warm stone, ambient reflections, and a collection of objects become the setting for an exploration of the wider Trapnest universe.
Movement with weight

Camera motion follows a keyframed path, while a separate inertia system carries the energy of each gesture. Position and orientation settle at different rates, giving movement a measured, cinematic quality.
Objects as invitations

A cylindrical gallery, a layered journal of architectural plates, and tactile inspection stages turn browsing into a sequence of spatial encounters. The feeling of weight comes from a careful relationship between visual motion and sound.
Space as an interface
House offers an architectural way of thinking about interaction: circulation becomes navigation, objects become doors, and the atmosphere of a room becomes part of the story.

posts.title: Trapnest Design: From Sketch to Space
posts.description: A journey from pencil on paper into an interactive world, where camera movement and tactile shaders give an idea dimension.
posts.lead: The distance between an idea and a place is a change of perspective.
body: The sketch as a beginning
Trapnest Design starts with the intimacy of pencil on paper and opens into a spatial world. It treats the sketch as a threshold: a way of giving an idea enough form to step inside it.
A camera that feels alive

The original essay explores aerodynamic camera behaviour, colour relationships in Oklab, and tactile shaders. These systems support a coherent sensation of moving from a flat drawing into a place with depth.
Craft in the small details

The experience is shaped by relationships: how a gesture affects the camera, how colour carries through a transition, and how a surface responds when it is approached. Those details turn technique into atmosphere.
Drawing becomes inhabiting
Design belongs to the same enquiry as Architecture: how a digital medium can communicate the emotional quality of a space, rather than only its outline.

posts.title: Trapnest Floral: A Living Spatial Garden
posts.description: A living spatial garden shaped by fluid optics, autonomous motion, reflective water, and a close attention to atmosphere.
posts.lead: A garden is a composition that never quite holds still.
body: An atmosphere in motion

Trapnest Floral brings together a studio, a mountain landscape, and an interactive playground. Fluid simulation, autonomous flight, and water reflections allow each setting to respond with its own character.
The intelligence of water

Planar reflections and gently distorted texture coordinates give the water its depth and movement. The original engineering essay shows how reflection, noise, blur, and colour grading contribute to a calm visual atmosphere.
A living point of view
A bee navigates through pursuit, steering, and analytical flight paths. Scroll and pointer gestures become part of a living sequence, while project surfaces bend with the energy of a drag.
Landscape as an experience
Floral suggests a useful architectural idea: a setting becomes memorable when its parts participate in the same rhythm. Light, movement, water, and interaction belong to one spatial composition.
